_note: Production editorial scaffolds only. Text values intentionally remain TODO so content writers can author final copy without implementation agents inventing interpretation prose.

selection_notes: Use only when all three selected-month scores remain within even-rhythm tolerance.
Do not use when one month materially exceeds the others.
Score layer includes selected primary/supporting event weight, station/convergence presence, and local monthly intensity.
First month materially exceeds the next two months.
Later months show declining selected-event weight.
Do not use when the distribution remains within even-rhythm tolerance.
Middle month is the clear local peak.
First and third months are lower enough to frame the middle month as a hinge.
Peak-month label and contour label must share the same scoring layer.
Third month materially exceeds the first two months.
Selected-event weight builds toward the end of the season.
Use when late-month growth is stronger than even-rhythm tolerance.
One month has a clear score lead, but the pattern is not specifically front-loaded, middle-hinge, or late-building.
Use when score variance is high and one month dominates the other two.
Attach the selected peak month in context.
Month scores descend in order across the season.
Opening weight is materially higher than closing weight.
Use when the contour is a true taper, not a single opening spike.
All three selected-month scores are low relative to the annual rhythm.
Visible reader-facing entries are sparse.
Use as an integration contour rather than pretending the season is evenly active.
Two months carry materially similar high scores.
The remaining month is lower enough to avoid an even-rhythm classification.
Use when the season has two distinct emphasized months.

rule_notes: Use when natal target belongs to angles, luminaries, or other configured primary chart factors.
Customer-facing label must not expose score values or developer terminology.
Use when duration and structural score qualify an event as a long-cycle carrier.
Detailed ranking explanation belongs in methodology, not repeated event prose.
Use when profections, cazimi, returns, progressions, solar arc, or convergence rules reinforce a selected event.
Requires traceable source method IDs in internal metadata.
Use when houses, angles, Vertex, or directed angles depend on exact birth time.
Suppress or soften when birth-time confidence is not exact.
Use for Tier B events retained as compact reinforcement or timing notes.
Must not imply the event is a full primary interpretation.

selection_notes: Use when annual headline and dominant long cycle are related but not identical.
Bridge must cite annual_theme_id, dominant_cycle_id, and supporting_event_ids.
